name: Hong Kong
meta: Tsim Sha Tsui, Jordan and Yau Ma Tei on the Kowloon side, with Central, SoHo and Sheung Wan across the harbour.

must.line: Steamed and fried small bites with tea: har gow, siu mai, char siu bao, ordered off a trolley or a tick sheet.
Crisp, lacquered skin over rich meat, best over rice noodles in broth. The char siu is the other must.
Thin springy egg noodles and prawn wontons in a small bowl of clear, savoury broth.
Warm, wobbly egg custard in a crisp pastry shell, Hong Kong's favourite snack.
A sweet bun with a crackly sugar top, no pineapple in it, split hot with a slab of cold butter.
Strong black tea strained through a cloth and mixed with evaporated milk, silky and punchy.
Rice cooked in a clay pot until a crunchy crust forms, topped with sausage or meats and sweet soy.
A hot sheet of crisp edged bubbles, soft inside, eaten straight from the bag.

items.one: Crispy chilli crab and flaming duck, three minutes away
items.fits: Tue 27 dinner in Tsim Sha Tsui at 20:45, straight off the Avenue of Stars. Book a 21:00 table so you are not rushed after the cruise.

items.one: Classic wonton noodles in Jordan, open past midnight
items.fits: Tue 27 dinner if you would rather keep it casual: open to 00:30, no booking, and on the way to Temple Street if you have the energy. Also works Thu 29 before the market.

items.one: Michelin starred Cantonese, 25 floors above the harbour
items.fits: Wed 28 big dinner at 19:30. A short walk from the Star Ferry, and the Mandarin Oriental is a five minute walk from the bars. The pick for views and occasion.

items.one: Apple wood Peking duck in a glamorous bank basement
items.fits: Wed 28 big dinner at 19:30. The pick for the best duck and the most theatre. Pre-order the duck when you book.

items.one: Loud, fun modern Cantonese in SoHo
items.fits: Wed 28 big dinner if you want a party rather than polish. Right in SoHo, so the bars are steps away afterwards.

items.one: Stocking strained milk tea and a pork chop bun
items.fits: Wed 28 at 14:00, right at the bottom of Graham Street Market as you arrive in Central. Or Thu 29 for a quick lunch. Closed Sundays, which is no problem for you.

items.one: Michelin starred roast goose on noodles
items.fits: Thu 29 lunch in Central at 14:00, off the train from Tung Chung, before the 15:45 Peak Tram. Hong Kong Station to Stanley Street is about ten minutes' walk, and 14:00 misses the lunch rush.

items.one: The city's best egg tart, sourdough crust, with coffee
items.fits: Wed 28 egg tart and coffee stop at 16:30, instead of Tai Cheong. Up Hollywood Road from Man Mo Temple to Staunton Street, then down to the Star Ferry for 17:15. Takeaway, so eat it on the escalator steps.

items.one: Claypot rice on Temple Street, crisp crust and all
items.fits: Thu 29 Temple Street dinner at 19:30. Order the claypots first, they take 20 minutes, then browse the stalls after.

items.one: Old style yum cha with trolleys and harbour views
items.fits: Fri 30 yum cha at 12:30, the classic trolley option. Star Ferry across, then five minutes' walk. Call to book or arrive by 12:15. Back by Star Ferry for the spare window.

items.one: Refined Michelin dim sum at The Peninsula
items.fits: Fri 30 yum cha at 12:30, the upscale option. Ten minutes' walk from the hotel, so no harbour crossing on your last day.

items.one: Dim sum on the 2nd floor of your own hotel
items.fits: Fri 30 yum cha at 12:30, the near TST option: zero travel, and the easy choice if the pool runs long. Also a fallback dinner on any night.

items.one: Cantonese roast meats in Elements, below Ozone
items.fits: Fri 30 dinner at 19:15, straight down from Ozone in the same building. Tell them you need to leave by 20:15 for the airport.

items.one: Hot egg waffle from a Michelin street food counter
items.fits: Any afternoon or evening walk near the hotel. Good on Tue 27 after the promenade, or Fri 30 in the spare window.

items.one: Pineapple bun with a slab of butter, the original
items.fits: Thu 29 after Temple Street for supper: two MTR stops north and open to 23:30. Or a breakfast swap for the lounge on Wed 28.

items.one: The World's Best Bar 2025, walk-in only
items.fits: Wed 28 bars in Central, after dinner. Expect to queue, it is part of the fun. Ten minutes' walk from SoHo or Central.

items.one: Award winning agave bar, tequila and mezcal
items.fits: Wed 28 bars in Central. Drop by at about 19:15 on the way to dinner to put your name on the waitlist, then come back after.

items.one: Harbour view cocktails at the Four Seasons
items.fits: Wed 28 if you want a seat and a view rather than a queue. Two minutes from the Star Ferry pier, so it works before the ferry home.

items.one: Dark spirits and live jazz at the Rosewood
items.fits: Tue 27 late, or Thu 29 at 21:30 instead of going straight back to the hotel. Ten minutes' walk along the waterfront.

items.one: Harbour view bar at the top of your hotel
items.fits: Any evening at 20:00 for the light show, or a rainy afternoon. Handy on Fri 30 if Ozone is clouded in.

items.one: Chinese art with harbour windows, free entry
items.fits: Fri 30 spare window at 14:00, five minutes from the hotel. Closed Thursday.

items.one: Timber nunnery and a Tang style garden
items.fits: Fri 30 spare window at 14:00, about 25 minutes by MTR. Go early in the window so the nunnery halls are still open.

items.one: Street stalls, sneakers and the Goldfish Market
items.fits: Fri 30 spare window, or a swap for Temple Street on Thu 29 evening. Three MTR stops north.

items.one: Floodlit Happy Valley racing, not on your dates.
items.fits: No Happy Valley meeting while you are here: Wed 28 racing is at Sha Tin, and the next Happy Valley meetings are Sun 1 and Wed 4 November.

items.one: Stilt house fishing village on Lantau
items.fits: Thu 29 after the Big Buddha, by bus instead of the cable car down. It costs lunch in Central and makes the 15:45 Peak Tram tight, so only if you skip the Peak or are on the Friday backup.

items.one: Mountains, beaches and the Big Buddha island.
items.fits: Already your Thu 29 morning. Tai O is the natural add-on.

items.one: The ridge hike with sea on both sides.
items.fits: Fri 30 morning instead of the pool if the weather is clear. Start by 09:00 to be back by 16:15. Take water and sunscreen.

items.one: Beach village at the end of the hike.
items.fits: Finish the Dragon's Back here for a swim and a seafood lunch, then bus back to Shau Kei Wan.

items.one: Head therapy, two minutes from the hotel.
items.fits: 11:00 to 22:00. Book by message.

items.one: Foot reflexology on Hankow Road.
items.fits: 10:00 to 00:30, so it works after dinner.

items.one: Foot and body massage on Granville Road.
items.fits: Open 24 hours. Good on Fri 30 after checkout while you wait for the airport.

notes: Book this week: the Wed 28 big dinner (Man Wah, Mott 32 or Ho Lee Fook; pre-order the duck at Mott 32), Hutong if you want it for Tue 27, and Spring Moon if that is your Fri 30 yum cha. The Chairman was named Asia's best in 2026 but now opens for lunch only and is very hard to book, so it is not an option for Wed 28 dinner. No Happy Valley races on your dates: Wed 28 is a Sha Tin meeting. Hong Kong Museum of Art is closed on Thursdays, so keep it for Friday. Coa is closed Mondays and Lan Fong Yuen on Sundays, neither of which clashes. Bar Leone and Coa take no bookings, so expect to queue on Wed 28. Hing Kee, Mak Man Kee and the Temple Street stalls are cash only. Some opening hours here come from older listings (Mammy Pancake, Lei Garden at Elements, Hutong): check Google Maps the day before.
